# Quick View Generate minimal HTML pages to review structured data in a browser. Use when terminal output is hard to read, when reviewing lists/tables/drafts, or when user says "show me", "make this reviewable", "quick view", or "open as webpage". ## When to Use - User wants to review output that's hard to read in terminal - Lists, tables, drafts, summaries that benefit from visual layout - User says: "show me", "view this", "make reviewable", "open as webpage" ## Output Rules **DO:** - Semantic HTML only: ``, `
    `, `
    `, `
    `, ``
- Use a light, readable color scheme with subtle background and borders
- Write to `_private/views/{name}.html`
- Open the file automatically with `open _private/views/{name}.html`

**DO NOT:**
- Add JavaScript unless essential for function
- Over-engineer or "make it nice"
- Use CSS frameworks

## Template

Every quick-view HTML file:

```html



  
  
  {title}
  


{content}


```

That's the base – three CSS rules plus a light background and colored header.

## Patterns

### List of items
```html

    Title
    

      
  
    • @username — action item
      • 

    
```

### Table (for columnar data)
```html
VersionDateStatusDeveloper
``` ### Expandable sections (for long content like drafts) ```html
@username — action 
Full draft text here...
``` ## Workflow 1. Identify the data to display (file, variable, recent output) 2. Choose pattern: list, table, or expandable sections 3. Generate HTML using template above 4. ` for each draft 4. Writes to `_private/views/drafts.html` 5. Notes: "File saved to `_private/views/drafts.html` – you can open it in your browser." Result: Browser opens (user opens manually), user sees expandable list of drafts, can copy each one.
